title: Best HR Software 2026: 5 platforms tested for a 75-person company
description: BambooHR, Rippling, Gusto, Workday, Deel — same 75-person company migrated to each.
lede: Five HR platforms. Same 75-person company. We migrated each, ran 30-day onboarding for 4 new hires, conducted performance reviews, and tracked which platforms a one-person HR team can actually operate without burning out.
methodology: Same company: 75 employees, US + 15 international contractors. 4 new hires onboarded per platform. Performance review cycle run. Tracked: time-to-onboard, employee self-service usage, time-tracking integration, payroll integration, total monthly cost.

sections.heading: Onboarding speed
paragraphs: Time to onboard one new hire (offer letter → all systems provisioned): BambooHR 2 hrs (manual coordination), Rippling 25 min (auto-provisions Slack/G Suite/equipment), Gusto 45 min (good payroll, basic HR), Workday 4 hrs (enterprise complexity), Deel 30 min (US hires), 1 hour (international).
Rippling's edge: it provisions software accounts (Slack, Google, GitHub, Notion) AND orders equipment AND handles I-9 paperwork. Most HR tools require you to do this manually.

sections.heading: Employee self-service
paragraphs: Employees can request PTO, view paystubs, update personal info, see org chart: all 5 support. UX quality: BambooHR > Gusto > Rippling > Deel > Workday.
Mobile app: BambooHR best, Gusto strong, Rippling functional, Deel adequate, Workday's mobile app is functional but feels enterprise-heavy.
Documents/policies portal: Rippling and BambooHR lead. Gusto has basic doc storage. Workday has powerful but complex doc management.

sections.heading: Total monthly cost
paragraphs: Monthly cost for 75 employees (HR-focused tier): BambooHR Essentials $99 + per-employee ($475 total), Gusto Plus $60 + $12 × 75 = $960, Rippling $8 × 75 = $600 (modular, scales with features), Workday HCM ~$1,500-2,250 (quote-based, $20-30/employee), Deel $49/employee for global payroll, $19/employee for US.
Hidden costs: Workday requires implementation partner ($30k-100k initial). Rippling charges per-module (HR, payroll, IT, finance separate). BambooHR's per-employee adds up at 100+ employees.

faqs.a: BambooHR for HR-focused SMB (under 200 employees) that wants best-in-class UX. Rippling for tech-forward companies wanting HR + IT + Finance unified.

faqs.q: Do I need HR software under 50 employees?
faqs.a: Under 30 employees: spreadsheet + Gusto payroll is usually enough. Past 30, you'll start needing structured PTO tracking, document storage, and onboarding workflows.

faqs.q: What about Deel for distributed teams?
faqs.a: Deel is best-in-class for international employees and contractors across 150+ countries. Handles compliance, contracts, and global payroll. Less ideal as primary HR for a US-only company.

faqs.q: Workday — when does it make sense?
faqs.a: Workday HCM is enterprise (500+ employees, $30k+ implementation). For most SMB, BambooHR or Rippling are better choices. Workday's complexity makes sense only at scale.

bamboohr-essentials.review: BambooHR Essentials is the right pick for HR-focused SMB under 200 employees. Best UX in category, employee self-service is best-in-class, mobile app strong. Pricing $99/mo + per-employee adds up at scale but the per-employee onboarding time saved is real.

rippling-platform.review: Rippling is the right pick for tech-forward companies wanting HR + IT + Finance unified. Auto-provisions software accounts, orders equipment, handles I-9. Modular pricing — pay for what you use. The fastest onboarding workflow we tested.

gusto-hr-plus.review: Gusto Plus is the right pick if payroll is your primary need and HR is secondary. Strong payroll, growing HR features (PTO, onboarding, doc storage). Less depth than BambooHR on pure HR but the bundle saves money for small teams.
cons: Outgrown at 100+ employees for HR-heavy needs

workday-hcm.review: Workday HCM is the right pick for 500+ employee enterprises. Enterprise feature depth (succession planning, learning management, advanced analytics). Implementation requires partner ($30k-100k). Overkill for SMB.

deel-hr.review: Deel HR + Global Payroll is the right pick for distributed teams with international employees and contractors. 150+ country support, handles compliance, contracts, and global payroll. The default for remote-first companies hiring globally.
cons: Less ideal as primary HR for US-only
